title: SSO SAML JIT: identity and email fall back to the NameID — an Entra ID IdP-initiated sign-in creates a second account whose "email" is an opaque persistent id, and the verified-domain binding is not enforced on JIT
body:
## Edition / version
ObjectOS Enterprise, cloud `main` built image (framework pin `e24136c2`, `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12), kit from cloud `main` `e3365dfa`, licensed. Live Microsoft Entra ID test tenant, non-gallery SAML enterprise app with the default claims. Browser walk-through for objectstack-ai/cloud#3666.

## Steps (measured)
1. Register a SAML provider `entra-saml` in Setup (IdP entity id `https://sts.windows.net/<tenant>/`, SSO URL, signing cert, groups attribute `http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/groups`, domain = the tenant domain). Allow JIT, then map the Entra group → an ordinary permission set.
2. **SP-initiated** sign-in as `objectos-entra4@<tenant domain>`:
   - the account is created with that email;
   - the group grant applies.

   This works only because the AuthnRequest asks for `nameid-format:emailAddress` and Entra answers with the UPN. Entra's email attribute is `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress`, not `email`, so the vendor's `attr(mapping.email || "email") || extract.nameID` falls back to the NameID.
3. Allow IdP-initiated sign-in, then open the app from Entra My Apps as the **same person**. There is no AuthnRequest, so Entra sends its default **persistent** NameID. Result:
   - a **second account** is created, `email = pov4hy2mt2…` (an opaque pairwise id, not an email address), name = the same string;
   - it is `idp_provisioned` and is **granted the mapped permission set**;
   - the person now has two ObjectOS identities with different grants and data.
4. Repeat with `OS_SSO_DOMAIN_VERIFICATION=true` (the EE default since cloud#3679) and the provider's `domain_verified = true`. The result is the same: the account is created although its "email" has no domain at all, let alone the verified one.

## Why it matters
- **Identity.** `accountId` and `email` come from whatever NameID the IdP sends. One person gets a different account depending on how they entered (SP- vs IdP-initiated, or after an IdP admin changes the NameID format), and the email becomes a random string.
- **Domain binding.** cloud#3679 turned domain verification on so that "an organization's IdP cannot JIT-create accounts on domains it has not verified". The verified domain is only consulted for *linking* (`isTrustedProvider` → `validateEmailDomain`); account creation never checks that the email is inside the provider's domain. A provider verified for `a.com` can therefore JIT-create accounts for `ceo@b.com`, or for an id that is no email at all. That pre-empts the real address in a single-org deployment.

## Expected
- JIT refuses (and linking refuses) any SAML/OIDC user whose email is not a syntactically valid address **inside the provider's verified domain**, with a clear refusal. Measure the OIDC path too; only SAML was measured here.
- The account key should not silently change with the NameID format. Request/require a stable format, or key on a configured attribute (`objectidentifier` for Entra).
- The SAML form lets the admin name the email/name attributes. This is the gap #32086 already lists for Okta. For Entra the defaults should be `…/claims/emailaddress`, `…/claims/givenname` and `…/claims/surname` (today the name also becomes the email).

Related: #32086 (SAML attribute mapping), #32085 (provider lifecycle).
